subject: Next steps: cost target & burst/overage terms for FinLytics POC
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya@finlytics.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & pricing inputs from today's discovery call

Hi Maya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we stay in sync: 

- What we heard: FinLytics wants to run a 3-month POC for model-assisted insights across two pipelines (batch scoring and interactive chat). Baseline traffic estimate you mentioned: ~200M tokens / month, with day-level spikes up to ~5M tokens on heavy analysis days.
- Key constraint: procurement has a target unit cost of roughly $600–$800 per 1M tokens for the POC.
- Concern: you want the ability to absorb short, high-intensity bursts without committing to large reserved capacity up front.

As next actions, could you confirm the following by EOD tomorrow if possible: 
1) Confirm monthly baseline and expected peak-day token numbers (you mentioned June snapshot — attaching a template would help).
2) Budget range for the POC (is the $600–$800 /1M tokens the true target or a ceiling?).
3) Any hard rate-limit or latency SLOs we should account for in pricing (e.g., 95th p95 < 300ms for interactive flows).

On our side, I'm attaching a first-pass pricing workbook and a draft SLA so procurement can start reviewing commercial/operational assumptions. High-level pricing notes you should expect in our follow-up: 
- Committed (reserved) capacity gives the best $/1M token economics, with a built-in burst allowance for short spikes.
- Pay-as-you-go (no commit) supports instant scaling but has higher per-token unit price and can include burst guards to protect overall capacity.

Attachments: pricing_model_v1.xlsx, SLA-draft.pdf

If you prefer, we can do a 30-min price walk-through with Jordan and Karthik to run scenarios against your June traffic snapshot. Is Friday 10am PT ok?

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez

Hi Alex — appreciate the follow-up and the docs. Quick answers inline: 

1) Baseline: 200M tokens/month is our conservative baseline. 
   - Typical day: ~6.5M tokens/day.
   - Peak days (ad-hoc heavy runs): up to ~5M–7M tokens in a single day (we had two such days in June).
2) Budget: the $600–$800/1M tokens is our internal target for the POC. Procurement may try to push lower, but that range is what the product team expects.
3) Performance: interactive flows should stay responsive — p95 ideally < 400ms. Batch jobs are less sensitive.

Procurement timeline: we need commercial language + simple SOW to start an internal purchase order conversation — ideally within 2 weeks. I'm attaching a June traffic snapshot for reference.

One more question: if we stay pay-as-you-go but have bursts like the ones above, what does Redwood do in the first 24 hours of the spike — do you auto-burst and bill at overage rates immediately, or is there a soft quota and notification window?

Thanks — Maya
Maya Patel

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 24 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up & pricing inputs from today's discovery call

Alex / Jordan — draft answers below. Quick assumptions: baseline = 200M tokens/mo, monthly billing period, peaks up to ~7M tokens single-day. Pricing shown as $/1M tokens (net) — list prices subject to commercial negotiation.

Option A — Small Reserved Commit (recommended for predictable economics):
- Commit: 200M tokens / month (matches baseline).
- Unit price on commit: $650 per 1M tokens (effective POC price).
- Burst allowance: automatic burst credit up to 50% of commit (i.e., +100M tokens) usable for up to 3 consecutive days per month without switching to overage pricing. Bursts beyond this are charged at overage rate.
- Overage: $900 per 1M tokens beyond commit + burst credits.
- Operational guardrails: soft per-minute token rate limit (e.g., 1.5x baseline RPS) and a 10-minute buffer notification before enforced throttling; we can relax buffer for the POC with a signed surge addendum.
- Notes: Best unit economics and simplest for procurement. We can offer a 10% one-time onboarding credit for the first month.

Option B — Pay-As-You-Go with Measured Burst (no commit):
- No monthly commit.
- Base unit price: $1,100 per 1M tokens.
- Auto-burst behavior: we allow short bursts up to 25% over the 7-day moving average without pre-approval; beyond that, requests will be allowed but billed at an elevated overage tier.
- Overage tiers: 0–25% over avg = billed at base price; 25–100% over avg = $1,500 per 1M tokens; >100% = negotiated emergency surge rate (we can throttle at this point).
- Throttling policy: if consumption threatens cluster stability, automated rate limiting applies per-minute; we provide alerting and a manual override path via support team.
- Notes: Higher unit cost but zero upfront commitment — suitable if procurement can't sign quick.

Other commercial levers we can offer: multi-month commit discount (15% off for 6-month POC), temporary surge bucket purchase (one-time top-up priced at $1,000 per 1M tokens to cover an anticipated run), or a blended hybrid (smaller commit + top-up bucket).

Recommended next steps:
1) I can convert Option A/B to a two-page commercial term sheet + SOW sketch.
2) If they want immediate burst comfort, offer a short-term surge bucket (one-time prepaid) while commit is negotiated.
3) Jordan/Alex to schedule the price walk-through and include procurement; I'm happy to join.

I'll attach a quick term sheet draft and the commercial worksheet for your review.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Pricing | Redwood Inference
